title: Sore Throat
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with sore throat, cough, rhinorrhea, hoarseness, conjunctivitis, and low-grade fever. Viral features (cough, rhinorrhea, conjunctivitis) make strep less likely. Centor criteria: no tonsillar exudates, no tender anterior cervical LAN, cough present, no fever → score 0-1 = no testing needed. Most pharyngitis is viral (adenovirus, rhinovirus, EBV, influenza). Management: supportive care — acetaminophen/NSAIDs, fluids, rest, throat lozenges, salt water gargles. NO antibiotics. Avoid unnecessary antibiotic prescribing — contributes to resistance. If Centor criteria score ≥3 → rapid strep test. If positive → treat as GAS pharyngitis. If negative → supportive only.

stacks.label: Centor criteria
stacks.finding: Cough, no fever, no exudates, no LAN = viral.
